results.evidence: `resolve_untagged_followup_mode` now returns `get_stored_untagged_followup_mode(integration, slack_user_id) or UntaggedFollowupMode.ASK`. `get_stored_untagged_followup_mode` returns None when the row is missing or the field is empty (`stored = row[...] if row else None` … `return None`). In `request_untagged_followup_confirmation_activity`, ASK falls through to `_post_untagged_followup_prompt(...)`, which posts the private `chat_postEphemeral` prompt.

A stored value that matches a known mode is returned unchanged: `if stored in UntaggedFollowupMode.values: return UntaggedFollowupMode(stored)`. The activity keeps the same branches: `if mode == UntaggedFollowupMode.AUTO: return False` and `if mode == UntaggedFollowupMode.NEVER: ... return True`. An explicit ASK still reaches the prompt. The NEVER branch applies to every replier, the thread creator included.

The default-saving buttons are only added when `offer_default = (slack_user_id == mapping.mentioning_slack_user_id and get_stored_untagged_followup_mode(...) is None)`. Any replier who is not the thread creator gets only "Yes, take a look" / "No thanks", with no way to save a default. So the prompt does not generally let the replier record a default for future untagged follow-ups.

`_build_home_view` passes `untagged_followup_mode=stored_followup_mode or UntaggedFollowupMode.ASK` and `untagged_followup_mode_unset=stored_followup_mode is None`. Because that value is never None, the section always renders. The picker's `initial_option` is chosen by `o["value"] == mode.value` (ASK), and the hint reads "You haven't picked yet, so I ask in the thread."

`get_stored_untagged_followup_mode` returns None for a value it doesn't recognise ("a value we no longer recognise all count as 'never picked'"). `resolve_untagged_followup_mode` then returns `... or UntaggedFollowupMode.ASK`, so those users now get prompted instead of falling back to NEVER.

The prompt's context text is fixed plain text: "You can change it any time under *Thread follow-ups* on my Home tab." It builds no link, even though `app_home_url` is imported in api.py. The line is also only shown when `offer_default` is true.

The patch changes no quota or AI-credit handling. Whether the workflow already stops unconfirmed untagged replies silently, while posting a denial for mentions and confirmed replies (`untagged_followup_confirmed=True` is passed when a reply is confirmed), depends on workflow code that isn't shown.

result:
Unset follow-up preferences now get the prompt. Before, a missing setting counted as "never", so these replies were dropped at the webhook with no message. Now a missing setting counts as "ask": the reply goes through the usual classifier, and if it looks meant for the agent, the replier gets a private prompt in the thread. People who already chose "auto", "ask" or "never" see no change. I haven't run the tests or the linters: `ruff` isn't installed here, and the only check I ran was a Python syntax compile, which passed. No migration is needed, because the column was already nullable.

**Whose setting counts:** the code already uses the setting of the person who started the thread, and I kept that. So the "save a default" option only appears when the replier is that person and has never chosen. Anyone else replying in such a thread gets just the one-off Yes/No question. Saving a default for them would change their own threads, not this one, so I left it out. If you meant the setting to belong to whoever replies, that's a bigger change to the routing — say if you want it.

**What changed:**
- **Settings lookup** (`services/slack_settings.py`): a never-chosen setting now resolves to "ask". I added one helper that tells "never chosen" apart from a real choice, and one that saves the setting without wiping the user's other settings.
- **Prompt** (`api.py`): when offered a default, the prompt gets two extra buttons, "Yes, and always pick them up" and "No, and don't ask again", plus a line pointing to *Thread follow-ups* on the Home tab.
  - Both buttons do the same thing as Yes/No for this message and also save "auto" or "never" as the default.
  - Before saving, the click handler re-checks that the clicker started the thread, so a stale or forwarded prompt can't change anyone else's setting.
  - "Always" saves before the existing "turned off while the prompt was waiting" check, so the newer click wins.
- **Deciding whether to offer a default** (`activities/messaging.py`): it's offered only when the replier started the thread and has never chosen.
- **Home tab** (`services/slack_app_home.py`): the *Thread follow-ups* picker was already there. For people who haven't chosen, it now starts on "Ask them first" and says "You haven't picked yet, so I ask in the thread." The Home-tab picker now saves through the same helper.
- **Model comments** (`models.py`): updated to say an unset setting means "ask".

**Tests:**
- Updated the tests that expected an unset setting to mean "never", in `test_slack_settings.py` and `test_thread_message_routing.py`.
- Added cases for:
  - the prompt being offered to the thread starter but not to other repliers;
  - "always" sending the message and saving "auto";
  - "don't ask again" dropping it and saving "never";
  - a non-starter's click saving nothing;
  - the Home-tab "haven't picked yet" text.
